fields.subnational_unit: Nepal (national, with provincial and local-government roles)
fields.population: Nepal's population and WASH sector institutions (federal, provincial and local governments) 2000-2020
fields.sample_size: no stated search or selection: narrative review of national assessments, JMP/SDG 6 indicators and policy documents (2000-2020), with SDG 6 comparison across eight South Asian countries (Table 1)
fields.effect_measure: narrative review of WASH status, challenges and opportunities; descriptive indicators from national and JMP sources; no quantitative synthesis
fields.effect_estimate: National estimates show healthy progress in WASH access since 2000, but large urban-rural, rich-poor and gender inequalities persist at sub-national level. Constraints: lack of long-term infrastructure capacity, financial gaps, institutional and policy incompatibilities, overlapping agencies and unclear functions across the tiers of the federal structure, weak coordination, and few institutions dealing with climate risk to WASH. Proposes roles for central, provincial and local governments (climate-risk assessment, community-level adaptation) and private-sector involvement. SDG 6 comparison for Nepal: integrated water resources management 37% implemented; water stress 8%.
fields.model_type: narrative review with descriptive indicator tables
fields.study_design: non-systematic narrative review of the national WASH sector (no search strategy, selection criteria or appraisal reported)
fields.section: Full text (ACS ES&T Water 3(6):1429-1453, accepted manuscript): Abstract; Introduction; Global perspective; Overview of WASH in Nepal; challenges; roles of governments; opportunities
fields.exact_location: Abstract lines 13-26; Table 1 (SDG 6 status in South Asia) p6-7; institutional challenges section; roles of central, provincial and local governments p53-56

evidence_level: Secondary evidence: a narrative (non-systematic) review of Nepal's water, sanitation and hygiene sector 2000-2020 (national assessments, JMP/SDG indicators, policy documents), read in full text 2026-10-04. Inequalities persist; overlapping institutional mandates and weak coordination under federalism. No search, selection or appraisal method: the CASP qualitative tool applied earlier does not fit.
